## Activity

During April 2024, Central Eye Clinic completed 200 retinal image captures as part of routine service activity. The recorded activity provides the basis for monitoring image quality and the subsequent grading workload. The service should continue to maintain complete and timely records for each capture, including any issues identified during the imaging process.

## Image quality

There were 5 ungradable image sets, representing an ungradable rate of 2.5 per cent. This result should be reviewed through routine quality monitoring to identify any recurring operational or equipment-related issues. The clinic lead has requested that recurring camera issues are logged with the service desk. Clear logging will support follow-up, help identify patterns, and assist with maintenance or other corrective action where required.

## Grading

A total of 49 results were graded as referable. The median grading lag was 2 days. This information should be retained for service reporting and ongoing review of referral-related activity. The combination of grading outcomes and turnaround information will support local oversight of the screening pathway and help the clinic identify any emerging pressures affecting image review or referral processing.
